findings.title: unsubscribe crashes with NoMethodError when the user has no TopicUser record
findings.body: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, `TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` can return nil — for example users in mailing list mode who receive emails for topics they have never visited or interacted with, and therefore have no topic_users row. The very next line calls `tu.notification_level`, raising NoMethodError and returning a 500 instead of unsubscribing. This is exactly the population most likely to click a per-topic unsubscribe link. The action should create the record (e.g. via `TopicUser.change`) or handle the nil case.

findings.title: topicUnsubscribe route name does not match the template path, so the page renders nothing
findings.body: The route is registered as a top-level `this.route('topicUnsubscribe', ...)`, which makes Ember look for the `topic-unsubscribe` template (and the `topic-unsubscribe` controller/view, which is where the new controller and view files are placed). However the new template was added at `templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs`, which registers under the name `topic/unsubscribe` — i.e. the name a nested `topic.unsubscribe` route would use. Because the resolved template name doesn't exist for this route, visiting /t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe will render an empty page and the `stopNotificiationsText` controller will never be used. Either nest the route under the topic resource or move the template to `templates/topic-unsubscribe.hbs`.

findings.title: Unsubscribing a watching/tracking user only drops them to 'regular', so notification emails continue
findings.body: The unsubscribe logic sets the level to `regular` whenever the current level is above regular (tracking or watching), and only sets `muted` when the level is already regular or below. The most common case for someone clicking 'stop receiving notifications about this topic' is that they are watching or tracking it; after one click they are still at `regular` and will continue to receive notification emails (replies to their posts, mentions) for the topic, while the page displays 'You will stop receiving notifications for <topic>'. That message is now false. If the intent is a true unsubscribe, the level should be set to muted in one step; otherwise the copy must not claim notifications have stopped.

findings.title: Direct tu.save! bypasses TopicUser.change bookkeeping
findings.body: The unsubscribe action mutates `notification_level` and calls `tu.save!` directly instead of using `TopicUser.change`. As a result `notifications_changed_at` and `notifications_reason_id` are not updated, the `UserActionObserver` after-save callbacks are not fired, and no MessageBus `notification_level_change` message is published — so other open browser tabs of the same user will show a stale notification level for the topic, and any reporting/auditing on when/why the level changed will be wrong.

findings.title: No test covers the new %{unsubscribe_url} interpolation in unsubscribe_link
findings.body: The `unsubscribe_link` translation in server.en.yml now requires an `%{unsubscribe_url}` interpolation argument, but the only spec change passes `unsubscribe_url` into the builder without asserting that the topic unsubscribe link actually appears in the text body or HTML part. There is also no test that `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` behaves safely when `unsubscribe_url` is absent — with the new translation, any caller that sets `add_unsubscribe_link: true` without `unsubscribe_url` will raise I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument and break email delivery. Tests should assert the rendered link and the missing-argument behavior.
